3:description: "Product Owner flow-mode workflow: screenshots, Figma flows, product docs, schemas and plans turned into a checked Mermaid model of the right FigJam diagram type, written to a board and delivered as the board URL with a read-back line and the HVR self-scan line."
18:Flow-mode guidance for FigJam diagrams. The workflow picks the diagram type the reader's question needs, turns screenshots, a Figma flow, a product doc, a schema or a plan into a Mermaid model of that type, checks it, writes it to a FigJam board and reads the board back before replying.
22:**Scope:** Type choice, intake per input type, the model, the pre-write check, the quality pass, the write gate, the composed, generated and `fj` write routes, the hybrid extension, the read-back and the reply
26:**Hands Off To:** the vendored `../mcp-figma/` packet for `figma-ds-cli` mechanics and its mutating gate, and `../sk-product-owner/references/interactive-mode.md` when the type, the sources, the target file or the order cannot be settled from what was supplied
34:Provides the flow-mode workflow for drawing a diagram on a FigJam board. Flow Mode owns the route, the type choice, the intake, the model, the check, the gate, the read-back and the reply. The write composes a framed board from the checked model through one of three routes, and the board is the only deliverable.
41:- An architecture, a sequence of calls, a state machine, a data model or a dated plan
53:- **Thinking:** Standard energy, which caps the intake at three rounds, and Deep energy is five. Quick energy is zero rounds: it fills the Brief in Section 4 from the sources and the defaults rather than asking, marks each row it inferred `assumed` with what would settle it and sends one message with the rows, the chosen type and an offer to draw unless corrected. Just-do-it wording selects Quick and never Raw, which skips the phase flow. No energy skips the check or the gate, because they guard a write to a shared Figma plan
65:7. **Gate.** State the Brief's question and the outcome the board must deliver, so the yes covers the purpose and not only the destination, then the three glance lines `references/quality-rubric.md` Section 3 asks to be written before the model, the first glance the board must win, the second glance that advances it and the last glance that may wait. The first glance is the accented node on a user flow or a process, marked by its one required `style` line, and on any other type the node, message or task an optional `%% focus:` line names. The gate then gives the target plan and file, what will be written, any planned extensions, the calls the write will spend and the rollback in one message and waits for a yes. On the composed route the calls are `whoami` for the plan, `create_new_file` for a new board, the `use_figma` call that composes each diagram and the `get_figjam` read-back. Figma limits a Starter plan and a View or Collab seat to six tool calls a month. Read tools count against that allowance and some write tools are exempt, so such a user may spend the whole allowance on one or two boards. The file is a new file, which the write creates first, or the `fileKey` of a board this work already wrote. A FigJam file has one page and no write can add another, so a page is never the target. An earlier yes never carries over to a new board. The gate is its own reply, sent only after the playback's answer, as Section 8 sets out under The gate is its own reply
67:9. **Extend.** Only when the gate named an extension, add it through `references/hybrid-workflow.md`
68:10. **Read back.** Read the written board with `get_figjam` on the board id the write returned, never from memory, and compare it with the model as Section 7 and the type's reference set out. The composing call returns a screenshot of the whole board, which is the overview, and `get_figjam` returns the outline with a screenshot of each node. A node that needs its own view is read with `get_screenshot` and the node id from that read, because the tool fails without one. Then check the overview for stretching, a label cut off, overlap, a connector crossing, an edge that reads as joining the wrong node, a colour that does not match its entry in the key and whether the board answers the `userIntent` sentence. A finding there goes on a `Finding:` line of the reply, and it is fixed only by reshaping the model and recomposing after a yes, inside the two-attempt bound Section 9 sets. Section 7 names the read for each route. The rows that fail silently are read back the same way, one at a time and before the gate. Each provenance row whose class is not current behavior or whose edge is inferred gets one re-read of its source, and that row records the reason. A row that quotes a source line is not re-read
69:11. **Reply.** Deliver as Section 8 sets out
92:The pass offers three proposals, cheapest first, and none of them is a stop of its own. The outline, the two framings and the look ride in the playback, and the sketch is the checked model the gate shows, so the run still stops only at an intake round, the playback and the gate. Each proposal states what the sources already show and a recommended answer with a one-line reason, so a user who does not know can accept it, and the one answer to the playback settles them all.
96:- **The sketch.** The checked Mermaid model the gate shows in chat, never written to a board before the gate's yes, so the shape can be argued with before it costs a write
98:The look is settled last, in five proposed choices:
103:- Four critique questions the gate answers about the sketch, opening with where the eye goes first and whether that is the node the board most needs read
136:- **A named gap.** No question settles the need and no other type fits, so the need stays unmet and is named as a gap in the playback before the gate
138:The route taken is recorded against the need it settled. A later reader can then see why the board holds this type. A need left unmet reaches the reply's `Left out:` line as a named omission.
152:5. **Name every omission.** Every cut, every split and every point the sources left open is named in the reply's `Left out:` line, so the user sees what the board does not hold
192:- `assumed` when no supplied source answers it. The row names what would settle it, and the assumption is said back in the playback before the gate, where the user can correct it
203:A source evidences only the item kinds it carries, and an item it cannot carry is asked for or named as a gap rather than filled in. Every item asked for in this section is asked the way Section 5 of `assets/flow-templates.md` asks, with the AI's reading and a recommended answer. An unanswered one proceeds on that recommendation, marked assumed and named in the playback before the gate.
211:- The provenance table row for that label names the read it came from, and `read visually` marks a label whose only support is a plain look, in the model as well as in the read-back line Section 8 sets
219:- A `NAVIGATE` or `SWAP` reaction to another frame is a new screen. An `OVERLAY`, `SCROLL_TO` or `CHANGE_TO` reaction is a state of the same screen. An `AFTER_TIMEOUT` trigger is a system trigger, not a person's move
231:- Apply Doc Mode's authority order and conflict gate. When no source wins, ask the gate's one question, which source governs, with the AI's reading of the clash and the source it recommends. The answer decides, and with no answer the recommended source governs, marked assumed and named in the playback
232:- A proposal or unknown step is drawn with its status in the label, or left out. It is never drawn as current behavior
234:- A contradicted item is never removed in silence. It goes to the reply's `Left out:` line with both sources and the reason, or the gate's one question asks which source governs and that answer settles it. Nothing is dropped without a trace and no new line is added for it
237:**Schemas, code and plans**
239:- A gantt chart reads the plan's own dates and owners. A date the plan does not state is asked for, never estimated
241:- A call between two parts evidences an edge in a sequence or an architecture, and a plan's stated dependency evidences one in a gantt. A call evidences the order and not the reason behind it
294:Distance is asked with the other two dial settings, with the AI's reading of where the board will be read and a recommended answer. Unanswered, `Laptop` stands. The gate names the setting it drew at, so a reader who disagrees corrects it before anything is written.
315:- **Named omissions.** Every cut, every split and every point the sources left open appears in the reply's `Left out:` line, never dropped silently
340:Flow Mode composes the board itself. `scripts/compose_board.py` reads the checked model and fills `assets/compose-board.js`, and one `use_figma` call runs that code in the file the gate named. The call draws a framed board: the title and the subtitle, the diagram with its zones, every shape sized to its text and coloured by its kind, the routed connectors, a key of every mark the board uses and the source line, all on an 8 pixel grid. It draws every type in Section 3.
342:The route is a native MCP connection to Figma's server at `https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`, which Figma's own plugin declares in its root `mcp.json`. The connection comes from that plugin or from the client's connector. Code Mode holds no manual for Figma's hosted server here, and its `figma` manual runs Framelink's `figma-developer-mcp` instead. Whether Figma's OAuth-gated server would admit a Code Mode client is unverified. The vendored `mcp-figma` packet's wiring guide covers that Code Mode path only. The `allowed-tools` frontmatter of this packet names Code Mode as its only MCP tool. It waits for a live session to name the native tool prefix, because no source confirms one.
345:- Name the plan before the gate, because an account can hold plans that belong to other organizations. Call `whoami` and read the plans it returns. `whoami` says which plans the account holds and not which plan owns a board, so a plan it returns settles a new file only. On a new file one plan is named in the gate, and several plans become one question about which team the board belongs to, asked before the gate. A revision writes into a board whose plan was set when it was made, so on a revision the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it
346:- A new board starts with `create_new_file`, after the yes, with `editorType` set to `figjam`, `planKey` set to the plan the gate named and `fileName` set to the board's title. Load Figma's own skill for that tool first where the server offers one. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`, so the work stays on one board
353:- Read the written board back with `get_figjam`, as Section 7 sets out. When the server reports no read tool, the read-back is not possible and the reply says so. A read refused because the Starter plan or the View or Collab seat has spent its six tool calls for the month gives `Read-back: not possible` with that limit named, and the board is never called done
355:- The rollback for a new file is that file. The rollback for an existing board is to delete the one board section the write returned, which removes everything drawn inside it, through `use_figma` and only on a reply that names it or a yes to a question that names it, as the delete rule below sets out. A later session finds the boards an earlier one wrote by reading the tag on every section at the top of the page, `figma.currentPage.children.filter((n) => n.type === 'SECTION' && n.getSharedPluginDataKeys('productowner').length)`. Stop if the section to delete carries no returned id and no tag. With no read tool nothing is deleted, and the user removes the board by hand
356:- A revision request opens with a playback of the rows it changes, which waits for its answer before the gate. It composes the new board first, reads it back and then asks whether to delete the old board section found by its tag. The delete waits for its own yes to a question that names the old board by its title, so the yes that covered the compose never covers the delete, and with no second yes both boards stay. Composing first means a failed write never leaves the user with no board at all, and the tag means a revision in a new session replaces a board rather than drawing a second one beside it
357:- A delete of anything that was on the file before this write runs only on a reply that names the boards it removes, or on a yes to a question that names exactly those boards by title. A bare "yes" or "go ahead", the gate's yes and an answer to a question that named no board never delete such a board. The question lists every board the delete removes, and the delete removes those and no other. A board this conversation did not write, whether an earlier session or another person wrote it, is deleted only when the user's request is about that board, such as a revision of it, and never to tidy the page. Rolling back what this write added is not such a delete: it follows the rollback rule above, or the extension rollback in `references/hybrid-workflow.md`, each on its own yes to the deletion
358:- A board that holds two or more diagrams is planned before the first write, as `references/hybrid-workflow.md` Section 8 sets out
365:- The first call carries no `fileKey`, so the tool creates a new file. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`. Never call a separate create-file tool first on this route
366:- Read the diagram back with `get_figjam` by label, as Section 7 sets out for a board with no layer names. A failed or timed-out call is read before a retry, and when the first call failed there is no `fileKey` to read, so ask the user to look for a new file in their FigJam drafts before a retry
367:- This route adds nothing beside the diagram, because a title, a tag, a note and a deletion all need `use_figma`. The gate says so, and the reply names the missing tool. The rollback for a new file is that file, and on an existing board the user removes the diagram by hand
371:`figma-ds-cli` writes node by node into the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. It needs version 1.2.0 or later from the silships repository, because the npm build has no `fj` group, and its local daemon running. The vendored `mcp-figma/SKILL.md` owns the connection, the daemon and the mutating gate.
374:- On this route the target file is the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. Confirm with the read-only `fj info` that it is a FigJam board before the first write, and name it in the gate. Every FigJam verb fails on a design file
427:- When the provenance table lists items left out, the next line names them as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`
433:- A paired request, a route carrying `then: "FLOW"`, delivers the artifact first under its own mode's protocol: written, exported and read back. That reply ends on Flow Mode's playback, which waits for its own answer, with no ClickUp offer. Flow Mode then runs with that artifact as its product-doc source, under its own pre-write check and its own yes at the write gate
443:Before the model there is one full playback, and it waits for one answer. It states the Brief's question and its outcome, what each source settled, every row still open and every fact it assumed. That answer is not the gate's yes, because the gate asks about a write and the playback asks about the reading.
447:The playback is not one of the five reply lines. It runs before the write, and the reply states only the board, the read-back, the extensions, what was left out and the self-scan.
449:### The gate is its own reply
451:The playback and the gate are two replies, never one. The playback comes before the model, so its reply carries no Mermaid, no check result and no composed code. It ends on its one question about the reading, names no plan, lists no calls and never asks whether to write. The gate reply follows the playback's answer, and its one question asks about the write alone. No question is ever worded so that one yes covers both, such as a yes that confirms the reading and the write together.
453:Only a yes to the gate's own question writes. A yes to the playback, an answer to an intake round, a request to use the recommended answers or a yes to a question no reply asked never writes. Before the playback has had its answer, the reply to any of those is the playback. Once it has, and the gate has not been shown yet, the reply is the gate, and the write waits for the yes that answers it. A request to use the recommended answers sent after the playback counts as the playback's answer.
481:`use_figma` answers a call that carries no `fileKey` with "Failed to connect to MCP server 'figma'", which reads like an outage. Before calling the route down or falling back, check that the failing call carried the `fileKey` the gate named, and retry once with it. A call with no `fileKey` never reached the file, so this retry needs no `get_figjam` read first, unlike the failed call Section 6 sets out. Only a retry with the key that fails the same way counts as a connection failure, and the reply that says so names both calls.
487:### The plan or file is unclear
489:Stop before the write and ask. A board in the wrong plan is visible to that plan's members as soon as it lands. Where the server reports a `whoami` tool, call it before asking, because it returns the plans the account holds. On a new file a single plan resolves the gap and the gate names it. More than one plan means one question about which team the board belongs to. On a revision the board keeps the plan it was made in, so the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it.

365:- The first call carries no `fileKey`, so the tool creates a new file. Every later diagram of the same work and every revision passes that file's `fileKey`. Never call a separate create-file tool first on this route
366:- Read the diagram back with `get_figjam` by label, as Section 7 sets out for a board with no layer names. A failed or timed-out call is read before a retry, and when the first call failed there is no `fileKey` to read, so ask the user to look for a new file in their FigJam drafts before a retry
367:- This route adds nothing beside the diagram, because a title, a tag, a note and a deletion all need `use_figma`. The gate says so, and the reply names the missing tool. The rollback for a new file is that file, and on an existing board the user removes the diagram by hand
371:`figma-ds-cli` writes node by node into the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. It needs version 1.2.0 or later from the silships repository, because the npm build has no `fj` group, and its local daemon running. The vendored `mcp-figma/SKILL.md` owns the connection, the daemon and the mutating gate.
374:- On this route the target file is the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop. Confirm with the read-only `fj info` that it is a FigJam board before the first write, and name it in the gate. Every FigJam verb fails on a design file
427:- When the provenance table lists items left out, the next line names them as `Left out: <item>, <reason>`, so the user sees what the board does not hold. On a split or a cut, the reason names the detail level and the cut, such as `Left out: the retry path, split into a second diagram`
433:- A paired request, a route carrying `then: "FLOW"`, delivers the artifact first under its own mode's protocol: written, exported and read back. That reply ends on Flow Mode's playback, which waits for its own answer, with no ClickUp offer. Flow Mode then runs with that artifact as its product-doc source, under its own pre-write check and its own yes at the write gate
443:Before the model there is one full playback, and it waits for one answer. It states the Brief's question and its outcome, what each source settled, every row still open and every fact it assumed. That answer is not the gate's yes, because the gate asks about a write and the playback asks about the reading.
447:The playback is not one of the five reply lines. It runs before the write, and the reply states only the board, the read-back, the extensions, what was left out and the self-scan.
449:### The gate is its own reply
451:The playback and the gate are two replies, never one. The playback comes before the model, so its reply carries no Mermaid, no check result and no composed code. It ends on its one question about the reading, names no plan, lists no calls and never asks whether to write. The gate reply follows the playback's answer, and its one question asks about the write alone. No question is ever worded so that one yes covers both, such as a yes that confirms the reading and the write together.
453:Only a yes to the gate's own question writes. A yes to the playback, an answer to an intake round, a request to use the recommended answers or a yes to a question no reply asked never writes. Before the playback has had its answer, the reply to any of those is the playback. Once it has, and the gate has not been shown yet, the reply is the gate, and the write waits for the yes that answers it. A request to use the recommended answers sent after the playback counts as the playback's answer.
481:`use_figma` answers a call that carries no `fileKey` with "Failed to connect to MCP server 'figma'", which reads like an outage. Before calling the route down or falling back, check that the failing call carried the `fileKey` the gate named, and retry once with it. A call with no `fileKey` never reached the file, so this retry needs no `get_figjam` read first, unlike the failed call Section 6 sets out. Only a retry with the key that fails the same way counts as a connection failure, and the reply that says so names both calls.
487:### The plan or file is unclear
489:Stop before the write and ask. A board in the wrong plan is visible to that plan's members as soon as it lands. Where the server reports a `whoami` tool, call it before asking, because it returns the plans the account holds. On a new file a single plan resolves the gap and the gate names it. More than one plan means one question about which team the board belongs to. On a revision the board keeps the plan it was made in, so the gate names the board and states its plan only when the user supplied it.
